root_cause.text: The EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES constant in the ARM64 kernel page table header underestimated the required page-table pages because it failed to account for an additional segment split created by mapping [_text, _stext) separately with different attributes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies arch/arm64/include/asm/kernel-pgtable.h to increase EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES from (KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 1) to (KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 2), noting that commit 5973a62efa34 introduced a separate mapping for [_text, _stext) which requires one more page-table page than the previous allowance reserved.

intent_record.intent_summary: Increased early segment page reservation count to accommodate an additional text section split and prevent alignment boundary issues.
intent_record.what: Modified the EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES macro definition from (KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 1) to (KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 2) and added explanatory comments regarding the [_text, _stext) split.
intent_record.how: Increases the number of reserved pages during early kernel mapping initialization to accommodate an additional split and ensure SWAPPER_BLOCK_SIZE alignment boundaries are covered.

vuln_statements.explanation: This constant definition at line 76 was identified as the root cause of the vulnerability. It underestimated the required page-table pages by failing to account for an additional segment split created when mapping [_text, _stext) separately with different attributes. The value of 1 was insufficient to cover all necessary page table entries for this split configuration.
